liveProbe.reason: no turn was running; P0 forbids POST /api/turn because it appends to the production cli-main.jsonl

envelope.seq: u64 (global atomic counter, monotonic across the process)

envelopeExtensions.note: W513 per-session envelope: the TypeScript host adds these two keys to the frozen `{turn,seq,payload}` envelope (apps/studio/src/sse.ts: createStudioBus). The W744 parity test validates a real frame against `envelopeSchema` widened by exactly these keys, so an undeclared envelope key is a failure instead of an unnoticed drift.

lagged.trigger: a slow client is dropped by the broadcast channel (capacity 512)
lagged.semantics: the stream does NOT close; the client receives one lagged status and continues consuming. Skipped events are NOT replayed. `payload.dropped` (declared under `payloadExtensions.status`) is the cumulative number of frames this subscriber has lost, so a client uses it to decide how much history to re-fetch; it is a frame count, never a count of overflow bursts.

payloadExtensions.note: Keys the TypeScript host adds to an event payload beyond the frozen legacy table above (W513 per-session frames + W515 injection placements). They are contract too: `payloadExtensions.<event>` is the ONLY place a host-only payload key may be declared, and the W744 parity test fails on any produced key that appears in neither the event's `payload` table nor here. W785 added the `phase:"fallback"` value (a payload VALUE, not a new event name) and its five companion keys under `payloadExtensions.status`; the 9 event names are untouched (K5/D8). W1467 added `parent_id` under `payloadExtensions.tool` and `payloadExtensions.tool_result`: a run_code SUB-CALL row (the program SDK bridge call) is published on the same two events as a top-level tool, and the client indents it under the card whose id equals parent_id. The 9 event names are untouched. W1528 added the terminal event (9 -> 10 names) with its payload declared in the events table itself, like question - it has no LoopEvent producer, so there is nothing to extend.

status.session: string|null (the session the frame belongs to; null = process-level)
status.dropped: integer (lagged frames only: the frames this subscriber has ACTUALLY LOST, as a running cumulative total - each per-session bucket overflow discards that session’s whole backlog and the sum of the discarded frames is what is reported. A FRAME count, never a count of overflow bursts: the retired value conflated the two and counted overflow events, so at the production capacity of 512 a client that had really lost 1537 frames was told 513. The frame that TRIGGERS an overflow is never appended, so it is neither delivered nor counted. Because skipped events are NOT replayed this is the client’s only signal that frames are missing, hence the running total rather than a per-burst delta; the burst count is a host-side diagnostic on BusSubscription.droppedBursts and is deliberately not on the wire)
status.boundary: 'turn-start'|'step'? (the boundary that consumed an injected message)
status.effective_model: string (E §4.2.3 #4, W785: the model actually serving; present on a fallback frame and readable from /api/status.effective_model)
status.from: string|null (W785: the target that just failed and is being left behind; `phase:"fallback"` frames only)
status.to: string (W785: the target about to run; `phase:"fallback"` frames only)
status.attempt: integer (W785: index of the attempt ABOUT to run, §5.2 numbering)

tool.parent_id: string (W1467: the enclosing run_code call id; present ONLY on a sub-call frame - the row own id is `<parent_id>:c<n>`. Absent = a top-level call)

tool_result.parent_id: string (W1467: same as payloadExtensions.tool.parent_id - the enclosing run_code call id, present only on a sub-call result)

events.name: compact
events.note: envelope `turn` is ALWAYS 0 for compact events

events.name: question
events.source: W783: the user-questions service, while a turn is parked (host-emitted)
events.note: W783: emitted when the model calls ask_user_question, i.e. while the turn's slot is BUSY. The answer does NOT come back over POST /api/turn (that would be steering, and steering is only drained at step boundaries the parked call never reaches) -- it goes to POST /api/questions/{id}/answer. envelope `turn` is the SESSION-local turn number of the turn that parked.

events.name: terminal
events.source: W1528: the terminal handler (apps/studio/src/handlers/terminal.ts), relaying a sandboxed script(1) pty
events.note: W1528: the 10th event and the FIRST that is neither a turn event nor a host status frame. data is opaque terminal output (escape sequences included) and is NOT guaranteed to be a whole UTF-8 character at a chunk boundary; the client feeds it through a streaming UTF-8 decoder. Lossy under back-pressure BY CONTRACT (the bus emits lagged rather than blocking) - a slow client loses output instead of stalling the child pipe. envelope turn is ALWAYS 0: a pty is not a turn.

retiredDeadListeners.name: context
retiredDeadListeners.note: HISTORICAL, NOT CURRENT STATE: the frontend used to subscribe to `context` (and `inbox`), neither of which this bus can ever emit -- apps/studio/src/sse.ts asserts SSE_EVENT_NAMES on every emit, so those two subscriptions could never fire while looking wired. W1479 removed both from apps/web/src/sse.ts EVENT_NAMES; the rationale is recorded at apps/web/src/sse.ts:69-75.
retiredDeadListeners.status: fixed: no frontend listener remains (verified: EVENT_NAMES is status, text, thinking, tool, tool_result, done, compact, question, terminal)
retiredDeadListeners.guardedBy: apps/web/tools/check-sse-events.mjs (fails if the frontend ever listens to a name the server cannot emit)
